subject: general
question: The arithmetic mean of the observations 69, 60, 39, 58, 55, 31, 84, 64 and 80 is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Assume an **assumed mean** of 60 and calculate **deviations**.

Net deviation = +9 + 0 − 21 − 2 − 5 − 29 + 24 + 4 + 20 = 0.

**Actual Mean** = Assumed Mean + (Net Deviation ÷ Total Observations).

Mean = 60 + (0 ÷ 9) = 60.

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given observations:** 69, 60, 39, 58, 55, 31, 84, 64, 80

**Number of observations (n):** 9

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2f3b258e95a61f462c914149633ef782cf6d15b0507fffb0851a6a46d759989f.png] 

**Formula Used:** Arithmetic Mean (μ) = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations)

⇒ Sum (Σx) = 69 + 60 + 39 + 58 + 55 + 31 + 84 + 64 + 80

⇒ Sum (Σx) = 540

⇒ Mean = 540 ÷ 9

⇒ Mean = 60

**∴ The correct answer is 60.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Arithmetic Mean

The sum of **deviations** of items from their **arithmetic mean** is always zero, i.e., Σ(xᵢ − μ) = 0.

Effect of Change in Origin

If a **constant** value 'k' is added to or subtracted from every observation, the **mean** will also be increased or decreased by 'k'.

Weighted Arithmetic Mean

When observations have varying levels of importance, the **Weighted Mean** is calculated as Σwᵢxᵢ ÷ Σwᵢ, where w represents the **weight**.</p
